parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Use the principle of conservation of momentum to explain why the initial velocities of nucleus Q and the $\alpha$-particle must be in opposite directions.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Determine the initial speed $v$ of nucleus Q.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Calculate the initial kinetic energy, in MeV, of the $\alpha$-particle.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.stem:
A graph of number of neutrons $N$ against proton number $Z$ is shown in Fig. 7.2.

{{figure:figure_7_2.png}}

Fig. 7.2

The graph shows a cross that represents nucleus P.

A nucleus R has a nucleon number of 242 and is an isotope of nucleus P.

Nucleus R decays by emitting a $\beta^-$ particle to form a different nucleus S.
parts.text:
On Fig. 7.2, draw a cross to represent:

1. nucleus R (label this cross R)

2. nucleus S (label this cross S).

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text: State the name of the other lepton, in addition to the $\beta^-$ particle, that is emitted during the decay of nucleus R.

stem:
A stationary nucleus P of mass $243\text{u}$ decays by emitting an $\alpha$-particle of mass $4\text{u}$ to form a different nucleus Q, as illustrated in Fig. 7.1.

{{figure:figure_7_1.png}}

Fig. 7.1

The initial speed of the $\alpha$-particle is $1.6 \times 10^7 \text{m s}^{-1}$.
